item.title: Above Bone — Fri Nov 13, 12:00 PM — Axis Gallery
item.description: ADERO WILLARD ABOVE BONE November 6–29, 2026 Reception and Artist Talk on Saturday, November 7, 5–8 PM Artist in the gallery on Sundays, November 8 and 29, 12–5 PM Axis Gallery presents Above Bone, an exhibition of ceramic sculpture by Sacramento artist Adero Willard, on view November 6 through 29, 2026. The exhibition brings together new work and pieces never before shown in Sacramento or on the West Coast. Join the artist for the reception and artist talk on Saturday, November 7, 5–8 PM. ABOUT THE EXHIBITION Above Bone refers to what is beneath, the layers, and what emerges. Clay sculptural vessels of heads and body forms explore death, regeneration, new growth, and what is hidden. Adero wrestles clay into expressive forms and creates surfaces dense in color and pattern: thick clay and delicately etched vines and flowers. The forms are camouflaged, as if growing from or being returned to the ground. Layered colorful patterns, resists, and luster build up over multiple firings. Pat

item.title: Capturing Memories of Grief/Capturando Memorias del Duelo — Fri Nov 13, 12:00 PM — Axis Gallery
item.description: SUMMER VENTIS AND LINA RINCÓN CAPTURING MEMORIES OF GRIEF/CAPTURANDO MEMORIAS DEL DUELO November 6–29, 2026 Reception on Saturday, November 7, 5–8 PM The project, “Capturing Memories of Grief,” is a collaboration between artist Summer Ventis, sociologist and poet Lina Rincón, and you. Together, we explore the intersection of grief, memory, and image. We began this project with a conversation about our shared experience of losing a parent. When we recalled these experiences, we learned that we both had memories that centered around images, photographs, and the process of photography as a way to make sense of and process the meanings of our loss. In Fall of 2025, we began a series of grief-themed tours of works in the Crocker Art Museum’s collection. At the end of the tours, participants gathered to share and document our memories of grief and loss and how they connect with different types of images. item.title: Live@DCC Free Noon Concert - Tres Musicos! — Fri Nov 13, 12:00 PM — Davis Community Church (DCC)
item.description: Live@Dcc Free Noon Concerts presents on Friday, November 13, Tres Musicos: a trio consisting of Anita Felix, violin; Curtis Kidwell, Oboe; and John Cozza, piano. They will perform works by Ravel, Respighi and Turina, all arranged by Curtis Kidwell. John Cozza, Curtis Kidwell and Anita Fetsch Felix each performed in the Sacramento area, occasionally crossing paths through various orchestral and chamber music performances, but it was a cookbook purchased by Curtis Kidwell that ultimately brought them together. The cookbook of Spanish cuisine contained a CD of wonderful Spanish guitar pieces that sparked a curiosity. Upon investigation, Curtis discovered a treasure trove of of music composed by Spanish composers living in Paris between World War I and World War II. In 2012 Curtis Kidwell embarked on a compositional odyssey to arrange these gems into chamber works for violin, oboe and piano, which marked the start of our collaboration. item.title: The Grand Soirée: BizLink Alliance 2nd Annual Gala — Fri Nov 13, 5:00 PM — Project Church
item.description: BizLink Alliance invites the community to The Grand Soirée, its 2nd Annual Gala, on Friday, November 13, 2026, from 5 to 9 PM at Project Church, 1200 2nd Street, in Old Sacramento. It is an evening to celebrate with members and the wider Sacramento-area business community: dinner, a silent auction, live entertainment, a DJ and giveaways. The gala gives back to 5.14 Justice, a Sacramento nonprofit that provides food, Christmas gifts and college scholarships for underserved kids and families. Dress code: formal evening attire. Elegant and black tie are welcome but optional. Tickets: individual $85 ($65 for members); two-ticket package $150 ($120 for members). Sponsorship packages are also available. Info and tickets: https://www.bizlinkalliance.com/gala Can’t wait until the gala? Visit a BizLink Alliance chapter first. item.title: Manetti Shrem Museum: Together Again, 1960–2026, Perspectives from UC Davis’ Fine Arts Collection — Fri Nov 27, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description: Together Again inaugurates the Manetti Shrem Museum’s ongoing collection galleries. This exhibition highlighting the collection will be on long-term view, accompanied by temporary exhibitions each fall and winter. The ongoing collection galleries trace a history of art forged from UC Davis and throughout Northern California. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, this presentation proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri. item.title: Blood on the Clocktower at Blue Note — Wed Dec 2, 5:00 PM
item.description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering The first Wednesday of every month, we play _Blood on the Clocktower_, a social deduction game in the vein of Werewolf/Mafia/The Resistance, with a few twists!
We'll have a circle of chairs reserved inside Blue Note, near the back, with a Yolo County Board Game Gathering sign on the table. Just say hello, and we'll show you some games, pull some players together, and get to having fun!
We also usually have a few tables of players playing other board games, if social deduction isn't your bag!
Get a feel for Blood on the Clocktower here: https://youtu.be/4sfa8_kNxsQ

item.title: Out of Line: Art at the Edge — Fri Nov 13, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
Inspired by conceptual artist Bruce Nauman’s video work “Dance or Exercise on the Perimeter of a Square (Square Dance), 1967–68,” this exhibition explores Davis as a site of both artistic practice and political protest. Mike Henderson, Ester Hernandez, Malaquías Montoya, Bruce Nauman, Nancy Rubins, Dorothy Wiley and the student artists of UC Davis’ Third World Forum engage with film, print and performance to confront who they were and what their work meant in a world of radical change. They made work wherever and however they could: in collaborative workshops, student newsrooms, kitchens and living rooms. While rooted in the politics of the late 20th century, “Out of Line” finds renewed meaning in the present day.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Together Again, 1960–2026: Perspectives from UC Davis' Fine Arts Collection — Fri Nov 13, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
This ongoing collection exhibition traces a history of art forged from this place. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, “Together Again” proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Human Relations Commission Meetings — Thu Nov 26, 6:30 PM — City Hall Community Chambers
item.description:
The Davis Human Relations Commission (HRC) meetings aim to promote mutual respect, understanding, justice, and advancing the human rights of all people. The Human Relations Commission meets on the fourth Thursday of each month at 6:30 p.m. The Commission takes a recess in July (no meeting in July).
Meetings take place in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. For more information on meetings, membership, resolutions, and more, visit the Human Relations Commission site.
The HRC makes recommendations around equity and discrimination in the City, and supports the City in preventing and addressing discrimination while promoting diversity, equality, and justice relevant to the goals and policies of the City Council.
To contact or send emails to the commission, email: HRC@cityofdavis.org
Source: Hate-Free Together

item.description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering Update 8/14/25: **We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)
We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.
Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.

item.title: DataLab Office Hours (in person) — Tue Feb 9, 1:00 PM — Shields Library
item.description:
DataLab offers free in person drop-in office hours during which UC Davis researchers can obtain data science help and advice on working with their data. During these short, just-in-time sessions we meet with faculty, students, postdoctoral scholars, and staff from all domains across the University. Depending on the nature of your question and our availability, it may be possible to schedule a longer follow-up consultation after your office hours visit.
Appointments are not required. Please complete the brief office hours intake form ahead of time to help us connect you with the right expert for your question.
Common office hours help topics include:
